To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
antibodies to antigens present on the surface of early S phase of plasmodial Physarum polycepahlum, when added to the surface of G2 phase plasmodium, advance nuclear divisions.

the mitotic activity of the plasmodium is regulated by factors present in the cytoplasm and that these factors are not present in the cytoplasms of plasmodial stages of the cell cycle which precede the mitosis.
the plasmodium of P. polycephalum contains factors with mitotic activities and these factors can be isolated by immunological methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of mitotic promoting factors from the plasmodeal stage of Physarum.
the identification of factors which advance mitosis in the plasmodia stage of the myxo-mycete Physaram polycephalum.
the immunological isolation and characterization of factors with mitogenic activity from the plasmid stage of the myxcornycete Physaram polycephalum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immunologically purified plasmoidal extracts of late G 2 phase, but not those of early S phase, contain factors which accelerate mitosis in Physarum plasmodia.
the G2 extracts contain a factor which is responsible for the advancement of nuclear divisions.
the G2 extract contains at least two factors, one of which is an immunologically active protein and another of which is not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunological approach is a powerful method for the isolation of mitogenic factors from Physarum polycehpalum plasmodia.
the immunological approach to isolation of factors which advance nuclear mitosis from G2 phase is a useful technique for the isolation of such factors from Physarum plasmodia.
the immunological approach was successful for isolating a mitotic activity from plasmodia and that the activity was associated with the antigens that appeared in late G2 phase plasmodial extract.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitosis in the plasmodia is advanced by a factor or factors present in the plasmodal extracts of late G _{2} phase.
the mitotic factors of Physarum can be purified by immunological methods.
immunologically purified G2 extracts are effective in advancing mitotic activity in plasmodial cultures of P. polycephalum.
